 status post bone marrow transplant in [**2194**] who has been in remission for his
 multiple myeloma. He has an indwelling portocath on the left and acutely
 developed superior vena cava syndrome at 9 P.M. last night.  Please evaluate
 for SVC thrombus and provide therapy.

 PROCEDURE:  Informed and signed consent was obtained from the patient with his
 wife present.  The risks and benefits were explained, especially the risks of
 TPA infusion.  The patient and his wife both expressed understanding and
 agreed to continue with the procedure.

 attdending radiologist present and supervising.  The right upper neck was
 prepped and draped in standard sterile fashion.  Local anesthesia was acheived
 with 1% lidocaine.  Using ultrasonographic guidance the right internal jugular
 vein was punctured with a 21 gauge micropuncture set under ultrasonographic
 guidance. A 0.18 guidewire was then advanced into the SVC with ease.  The
 needle was exchanged for a 4 French micropuncture kit.  The internal dilator
 and the wire were then removed.  A hand venogram was performed which
 demonstrated thrombus. After this 5 mg of TPA was slowly infused via a hand
 injection into the thrombus. Another hand venogram was performed which
 demonstrated a decrease in the amount of clot burden. Then a 0.35 glidewire
 was placed through the micropuncture sheath and into the IVC and the sheath
 was exchanged for a 4 French straight multi sidehole catheter. The catheter
 was placed within the thrombus and another 5 mg of TPA was infused directly
 onto the clot.  After this there was free flow of blood through the catheter.

 combination of suture, steri-strips and tegaderm. TPA will be slowly infused
 at 1 mg per hour through the catheter for a duration of 12 hours and then
 stopped. Simultaneously there will be a peripheral Heparin drip with 200 units
 per hour which will also start now and continue for at least 48 hours.

was stopped. He remained stable, with no additional thrombus or
signs of SVC blockage.

pain, fatigue, and weight loss over the 2 weeks prior to
admission.  This was concerning for relapse of myeloma.  Total

have a return of his fever 13 hours after his last dose.  The
fevers then recurred daily, and on some days occured for the
majority of the day. They seemed to worsen in length and
intensity as his course progressed.  After 2 days of febrility,
the vancomycin was restarted.  However, he did not defervese.

hardware from contamination. Multiple blood cultures were

infiltration.

 fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG), noncontrast CT images were obtained for attenuation
 correction and for fusion with emission PET images. The noncontrast CT images
 are not used to diagnose disease independently of the PET images.  A series of
 overlapping emission PET images was then obtained. The fasting blood glucose
 level, measured by glucometer before injection of FDG, was 103
 milligram/deciliter. The area imaged spanned the region from the skull base to
 the proximal femurs.

 Computed tomography (CT) images were co-registered and fused with emission PET
 images to assist with the anatomic localization of tracer uptake.  The
 determination of the site of tracer uptake seen on PET data can have important
 implications regarding the significance of that uptake.

 INTERPRETATION:  There is an FDG avid (maximum SUV 16.7) left upper lobe mass
 measuring approximately 2.7 x 5.6 cm within the medial aspect of the left upper
 lobe, immediately adjacent to the mediastinum.  A left prevascular node measures
 2.9x1.8cm and contains increased FDG uptake (SUV 12.4).  Several additional
 small prevascular nodes are subcentimeter in size and do not demonstrate
 increased FDG uptake.  There are at least two FDG avid nodes within the left
 hilum.  No contralateral FDG avid nodes are identified.

 Additional nodular opacities measuring up to 4 mm in diameter are seen within
 the left upper lobe superior and lateral to the mass, without abnormally
 increased FDG uptake; however, these nodular opacities are below the PET
 resolution.

 There is no focal abnormal uptake of FDG in the abdomen.  Within the gluteal
 crease, there is a focus of increased FDG uptake with maximum SUV of 3.8,
 associated with a tiny region of increased density in the subcutaneous fat of
 the left buttock.  Small bilateral inguinal nodes and a left iliac node are
 non-FDG avid.

 Physiologic uptake is seen in the myocardium, liver, bowel and GU tract.

 IMPRESSION:  1.  Markedly FDG avid left upper lobe mass with FDG-avid
 ipsilateral hilar and mediastinal lymphadenopathy.  Findings are consistent with
 lung cancer with nodal metastases.  2.  Additional nodular opacities within the
 left upper lobe do not display FDG avidity, but are below PET resolution.
 3.  Tiny focus of increased FDG avidity in left buttock could represent
 inflammatory process in skin and subcutaneous tissues.

Dementia.

history of multiple jobs.  History of drinking six or seven
scotches per day.  Nonsmoker.

unremarkable except for heart rate of 108.  Physical
examination is notable for positive Dupuytren's contracture.

Hematocrit was stable in the mid 30s overnight.  He underwent
esophagogastroduodenoscopy which was negative for any source

friable esophageal mucosa consistent with Barrett's

Protonix with follow-up with his primary care physician in

esophagogastroduodenoscopy for biopsies to confirm the visual
appearance of Barrett's esophagitis.  The patient is to
follow-up in six to eight weeks.

all his original outpatient medications in stable condition

 CLINICAL INFORMATION: 78-year-old woman with pelvic and abdominal trauma, and
 who had percutaneous nephrostomy tube placed recently. Subsequent CT study
 demonstrated malpositioned tube. Needs reposition of the nephrostomy catheter.

 PHYSICIANS: The procedure was performed by Dr. [**First Name (STitle) 3006**] [**Name (STitle) **] and Dr. [**Last Name (STitle) **] [**Last Name (NamePattern4) 179**]
 [**Doctor Last Name 180**]. Dr. [**Last Name (STitle) 179**] [**Name (STitle) 180**] the attending radiologist was present and
 supervising throughout the procedure.

 PROCEDURE AND FINDINGS: The patient was placed prone on the angiographic
 table. The left lumbar region and the preexisting nephrostomy tube were
 prepped and draped in the standard sterile fashion. A Bentson guidewire was
 advanced through the preexisting catheter. Multiple attempts to repositioning
 the preexisting catheter into the left lower collecting system were
 unsuccessful. This catheter was left with its tip in the soft tissue around
 the kidney as spontaneous drainage of urine- like fluid was still present.
 Thus, the decision was made that a new percutaneous nephrostomy tube placement
 should be performed.

 After local anesthesia with 10 cc of 1% lidocaine, access was gained with a
 22-gauge Chiba needle through the left lower pole calyx under real-time
 ultrasonographic guidance. Antegrade nephrostogram with contrast injection
 through the needle demonstrated adequate positioning in the collecting system,
 residual mild dilatation of the calyces and renal pelvis (less severe than
 before), and almost no contrast passing into the ureter. A 0.018 nitinol
 guidewire was easily advanced through the needle into the left collecting
 system. The needle was then exchanged for an AccuStick access system, which
 was followed by a 0.035 Bentson guidewire. The AccuStick system was removed
 over the wire, the tract was dilated over the wire with a 7 French dilator,
 and an 8-French nephrostomy tube was advanced under fluoroscopic guidance into
 the renal pelvis. The pigtail was performed and locked and a tube nehrostogram
 confirmed proper tube positioning and function, again with obstruction at the
 ureteropelvic junction or lower. The catheter was secured to the skin with 2-0
 silk sutures. The catheter was attached to external drainage bag.

 Since there was still small amount of urine drained through the preexisting
 catheter, this older catheter was left in place and connected to another
 external drainage bag. We will remove it later today, as soon as spontaneous
 drainage as stopped.

 COMPLICATIONS: The patient tolerated the procedure well and there were no
 immediate complications.
                                                             (Over)
